title: fix(sdk): retain saved connection after failed reauthorization
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16349

- Restores the saved SDK connection before processing a callback, so failed reauthorization exposes its error without dropping the prior in-memory key.
- Successful exchange still replaces the key; no-saved-key failures remain disconnected and callback cleanup is unchanged.
- Extends the existing provider failure table and successful-exchange controls. Three regressions fail before the fix; all 30 React SDK tests and 118 SDK tests pass afterward.
- Verification: strict typecheck, ESM/CJS/browser/declaration builds, Biome, independent provider tests, and native loopback exchange checks pass. Synthetic storage/responses only; no live account or Pollen changes.

gist.headline: The old key stays put
gist.blurb: A failed reauthorization can report its error without knocking out a connection that was already working. PolliProvider keeps the saved key in place until a successful exchange replaces it.
gist.summary: React SDK PolliProvider restores the saved connection before processing a reauthorization callback, so a failed exchange reports its error while preserving the prior in-memory key.
gist.impact: Apps using PolliProvider retain their existing connection after failed reauthorization; a successful exchange still replaces the key, while failures without a saved key remain disconnected.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the React SDK's saved connection as a small key resting safely beside a retro terminal while an unsuccessful callback arrives as an error note. Polli, wearing a tiny tool belt, keeps the key in place and reads the note; code-plants and a lime-green glow make the scene feel calm rather than alarming.
